cultural.vision_reason: This is a mid-20th-century propaganda-style poster painting showing a mother in ethnic minority dress with her child before a Vietnamese steel factory, a modern political artwork depicting Vietnamese life (likely a Northern minority woman rather than Kinh, but painted within Vietnamese national culture); it is a contemporary painted composition, not archaeological or traditional court art.

physical.title: painting
physical.summary: Poster-paint and chalk under-drawing painting on machine-made paper. This poster depicts a mother resting her baby on her hip with a factory in the background. She is dressed in the costume of a peasant with headdress, jade bangle, green "ao dai" (traditional dress) and belt, typical of the minority people of the North in Thai Nguyen. This is probably the Thai Nguyen steel factory, the heart of Vietnam's heavy industry at War. Her child is plump, healthy, happy and bundled in the warm brightly coloured clothes of the minority costume tradition. Signed, dated and inscribed (in the mother's voice) with words from a famous Vietnamese poem.
